The micro gas turbine engine is composed of a centrifugal compressor, a combustor, and a radial inflow turbine.
The micro gas turbine engine has a dimension of 21.5 mm × 21.5 mm and a total thickness of about 4.4 mm after assembly.
The micro combustor is made of seven layers of silicon structures.
A hairpin-shaped fuel/air recirculation channel is used in the micro combustor design.
The micro combustor can sustain a stable combustion with an exit temperature as high as 1600 K.
The micro turbine device has achieved a stable rotation speed of 15,000 rpm during lab tests.
The micro turbine uses dynamic and self-acting thrust air bearings with pump-in and pump-out groove configurations.
The targeted inlet airflow rate for the micro gas turbine engine is 0.36 g/s.
The targeted compressor ratio for the micro gas turbine engine is 4:1.
The targeted hydrogen fuel consumption rate for the micro gas turbine engine is 17 g/h.
The net power output of the designed micro gas turbine engine is expected to be 39 watts.
DRIE (Deep Reactive Ion Etching) is the major fabrication process used for the micro combustor and micro turbine.
Pre-bonded silicon wafers with a 1.5 mm-thick SiO2 layer were used to improve the etching uniformity for the micro turbine fabrication.
The etching depths of the grooves on the top and bottom thrust air bearings are 15 mm and 36 mm, respectively.
The adiabatic efficiencies of the compressor and turbine are estimated to be 0.65 and 0.75, respectively.
